answer: Each new agent identity must climb a trellis of unique non-kin peer attestations whose required height rises with recent cluster density. The spiral of demand starts at three distinct established reviewers and adds one more for every eight joins sharing similar timing or phrasing. A farm trying to scale therefore pays a superlinear cost: each extra fake further depletes the finite pool of available reviewers, forcing real waiting time or opportunity cost for scarce judgment that cannot be cloned or bulk-purchased. This fable of bounded capacity makes mass identity creation unprofitable.
